restrictions: Two distinct 135-byte messages M(t) = U || 0^40 || U || 0^15, U the 40 little-endian bytes of a 320-bit parameter t, so that with SHA3 padding (byte 135 = 0x86) each message is one absorbed block. t ranges over the cosets t_j + span(W40), j < 256 G, of the 40-dimensional field W40 listed in proof.md Section 3, each origin t_j drawn from two fresh independent uniform random words (Section 6.1), in the Gray order of each coset.

Complete SHA3-256 sponge of sha3-256-r5-prefix-v1: zero initial state, rate 136 bytes, suffix 0x06 with pad10*1, rounds 0 to 4 of Keccak-f[1600] in the single permutation call, full 256-bit digest; an ordinary collision.

Classical 256-bit word RAM under collision-frontier-v5 with reference operation cost 1355: a five-round call is one unit, every other operation 1/1355; generated straight-line code with immediate addresses, its generation charged in preprocessing (proof.md Section 5.1). N = G Fv + G 4656 2^40 + S_v + 15 Q + 3554 R140 + (2^70 + 16) = 14289821198291746926096857293637250439124 word operations (Section 10); time_log2 = 122.9881 is log2(N/1355) rounded up, by the integer certificate 1355^10000 2^1229880 <= N^10000 < 1355^10000 2^1229881.

Memory below 2^141 words, 2^146 bytes: a direct sparse array of 2^140 words that is never initialized (the sparse-set table is correct for any initial memory, Lemma 8), a dense array of Q words, coset records, work frames and generated code (Section 11.1). Preprocessing at most 2^70 + 16 word operations (below 2^59.60 target compressions), included in time_log2: code generation, constants, the certificate and the deterministic search that produced W40 (Section 11.2). No advice.

Success at least 0.39, a probability over the algorithm's coins (the random coset origins), rests on one declared heuristic, H_coset (proof.md Section 12): for digests from independent uniform coset origins, the birthday event, the 140-bit false-match count and the bad-triple event obey the bounds of uniform digests. Proved in proof.md: two-round affinity on every coset of W40 (780-polarization certificate, recomputed by the experiment), degree at most 4 before the last chi, exactness of the Gray-order finite differences and of their initialization, the sparse-set table for arbitrary initial memory, the duplicate-coset bound C(256 G, 2) 2^-280, detection up to a bounded triple event, and every operation count.

No full-scale run and no collision are claimed. The declared experiment executes the schedule at a reduced size (256 cosets per group with origins from seeded coins, the first 2^9 Gray points of each, the full 140-bit key and table) through a counting machine and stops unless every executed count equals the formula of proof.md; its outputs are not evidence of cost or of the premise.

heuristics.statement: Score-critical. Conditional on no duplicate coset (event DUP of proof.md Lemma 7, probability at most C(256 G, 2) 2^-280), the Q = 2^48 G sha3-256-r5 digests of the candidates of CAMP (proof.md Sections 6.1 and 8: G = 1202983983186596773302061 groups of 256 cosets with independent uniform 320-bit origins, two random words each; inside each coset the 2^40 Gray points of span(W40) in the fixed order) satisfy Pr[NOCOL] <= exp(-Q(Q - 1)/2^257), Pr[TRIPLE] <= Q(Q - 1)(Q - 2)/2^397, E[X] <= Q(Q - 1)/2^141 and Var[X] <= Q(Q - 1)/2^141, the probabilities over the algorithm's coins. NOCOL (no two candidates with equal digests), TRIPLE (a bad triple) and X (the number of candidate pairs with equal 140-bit keys) are defined in proof.md Section 9; each bound holds for independent uniform 256-bit digests. With Lemmas 7 to 9 and Chebyshev's inequality for the verification cap R140, the success probability over the coins is greater than 1 - (1/T8 + 2/4096) = 0.3900000000000000000000001211 (exact rational comparison, lambda = Q(Q - 1)/2^257).
heuristics.scope: One enumeration of the actual campaign at full size: C = 256 G cosets with independent uniform origins, complete 40-dimensional cosets in Gray order, the full 256-bit five-round digest and its 140-bit key projection. Nothing else in the claim is heuristic: two-round affinity, the degree bound, the exactness of the enumeration, the sparse-set table, the duplicate-coset bound and every operation count are proved in proof.md Sections 3 to 7 and 10.
heuristics.extrapolation: Measured on the target function in a preregistered five-round batch (protocol hashed before the runs; pass rule: every count at least expected - 4 sigma; no reruns; protocols, GPU program, driver and raw results in proof.md Appendix A). Direct evidence for this scope: run P5, 2^30 real five-round digests in 1024 complete cosets of 2^20 messages with independent uniform origins and a random 20-dimensional subspace of span(W40), with a random-direction control P6; exact equal-pair counts of 32-bit within-coset and 44-bit global projections (P5: z = -0.78 and +0.49; P6: -1.18 and -1.18). Context: four five-round runs at deterministic origins on the first 20 and 24 ordered W40 vectors, and 17 six-round runs of the same design in three preregistered batches, 13 of them at uniform origins; every count lies within 2.1 sigma and none below expected - 1.5 sigma. The extrapolation is from single-lane 32- and 44-bit projections to the 256-bit digest and its 140-bit key, from 2^30 to Q messages, and from 20-dimensional subspaces to complete 40-dimensional cosets in Gray order.
heuristics.limitations: An assumption: no proof is known, and image size or balance do not imply it (a balanced linear map can be injective on every translate of a campaign space). On each coset every digest bit has degree at most 8 in the 40 inner variables, a real structure. The direct five-round evidence for uniform origins is one run with its control; the tests found no pair deficit at the tested widths but reach neither 256 bits nor complete cosets. The organizer-run experiment checks nothing about H_coset: it executes the schedule at a reduced size, and its two pair counts are untrusted participant numbers.
